_**User (2026-04-27 09:35:21Z)**_

似乎關於如何update global agent skills 可以使用 `npx skills@latest update --global -y` 我們目前 @dot_agents/modify_dot_skill-lock.json.tmpl 是這種方式嗎？
具體實現方式是什麼
https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills
得仔細看看
https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills/issues/549

```
是的，`skills` CLI 通過 lock file 來追蹤版本，但要注意 **global vs project** 範圍對應的是**不同的 lock file**：

## Lock file 位置

| 範圍 | Lock file 路徑 | 對應指令 |
|------|----------------|---------|
| **Global** (`--global`) | `~/.agents/.skill-lock.json` | `npx skills update --global -y` |
| **Project** | `<repo>/skills-lock.json` (注意是 `skills-` 複數帶連字號) | `npx skills update --project -y` |

你的系統上：

- 全局：`~/.agents/.skill-lock.json` — 由 `chezmoi` 的 `run_onchange_after_40_install_global_skills.sh.tmpl` 在每次 `chezmoi apply` 時恢復（見 `AGENTS.md` 中 `project-knowledge-harness` 段落）
- 專案：`/Users/daviddwlee84/.local/share/chezmoi/skills-lock.json`（剛才讀到的那個）

## 判斷是否更新的機制

每個條目記錄三個欄位：

```json
{
  "agent-history-hygiene": {
    "source": "daviddwlee84/agent-skills/skills",
    "sourceType": "github",
    "computedHash": "1a9c8ad6...ced881"
  }
}
```

`update` 流程：
1. 從 `source` 拉取上游（GitHub repo）的最新內容
2. 重新計算該 skill 內容的 hash
3. 與 lock file 中的 `computedHash` 比對 — 不同就視為有更新並寫回新 hash
4. 沒有 `version` 欄位（不像 npm 用 semver），純靠**內容 hash** 判定

## 一個小細節

剛才執行 `npx skills@latest update --help` 時，CLI 自動掃了當前目錄並回報 `No project skills to update.`，因為你的 cwd `/Users/daviddwlee84` 不在 chezmoi 專案裡。要更新 chezmoi 專案的 skills 需要 `cd` 進去，或加 `--global` 走 `~/.agents/.skill-lock.json`。
```

```text
1	#!/bin/bash
2	# Restore globally-installed agent skills from ~/.agents/.skill-lock.json.
3	#
4	# The skills CLI (vercel-labs/skills) does not yet support `npx skills install -g`
5	# from a lock file (issues #283 / #549), so we hand-roll restore here:
6	#   1. The lock file itself is chezmoi-managed via dot_agents/modify_dot_skill-lock.json.tmpl
7	#      (merger that preserves per-machine state).
8	#   2. This script reads the merged lock and, for any entry whose
9	#      ~/.agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md is missing, runs
10	#      `npx skills add <source> -s <name> -g -y` to (re)install it.
11	#
12	# Trigger: changes to the merger script's $managed block (the source-of-truth list).
13	#   merger: {{ include "dot_agents/modify_dot_skill-lock.json.tmpl" | sha256sum }}
14	#
15	# Idempotent: a re-run with no missing skills is a no-op.
16	# See: docs/tools/agent-skills.md
17	
18	set -eu
19	export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$HOME/.npm-global/bin:$PATH"
20	
21	info()    { printf '\033[0;34m[INFO]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
22	warn()    { printf '\033[1;33m[WARN]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
23	success() { printf '\033[0;32m[SUCCESS]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
24	
25	LOCK="$HOME/.agents/.skill-lock.json"
26	
27	if [ ! -f "$LOCK" ]; then
28	  warn "Global lock file not found at $LOCK — skipping (chezmoi apply should create it)."
29	  exit 0
30	fi
31	
32	if ! command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
33	  warn "jq not installed; cannot parse $LOCK — skipping. Run \`chezmoi apply\` again after the base ansible role finishes."
34	  exit 0
35	fi
36	
37	if ! command -v npx >/dev/null 2>&1; then
38	  warn "npx not installed; cannot restore global skills — skipping."
39	  exit 0
40	fi
41	
42	# Collect names of skills declared in the lock that are missing on disk.
43	missing=()
44	while IFS=$'\t' read -r name source; do
45	  [ -z "$name" ] && continue
46	  if [ ! -f "$HOME/.agents/skills/$name/SKILL.md" ]; then
47	    missing+=("$name"$'\t'"$source")
48	  fi
49	done < <(jq -r '.skills | to_entries[] | "\(.key)\t\(.value.source)"' "$LOCK")
50	
51	if [ ${#missing[@]} -eq 0 ]; then
52	  info "All globally-managed agent skills present; nothing to install."
53	  exit 0
54	fi
55	
56	info "Restoring ${#missing[@]} missing global skill(s) via \`npx skills add ... -g\`"
57	for entry in "${missing[@]}"; do
58	  name="${entry%%$'\t'*}"
59	  source="${entry##*$'\t'}"
60	  info "  → $name (from $source)"
61	  # Note: -s <name> filters to one skill within multi-skill repos.
62	  # No -a flag → npx prompts auto-detect agents from $HOME/.<agent>/ presence.
63	  if npx -y skills@latest add "$source" -s "$name" -g -y >/dev/null 2>&1; then
64	    success "    installed $name"
65	  else
66	    warn "    failed to install $name (continuing)"
67	  fi
68	done
69	
70	success "Global agent skills sync complete."
71
```
</details></tool-use>

```text
1	# Agent skills (`vercel-labs/skills`)
2	
3	This repo manages [`vercel-labs/skills`](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills)
4	agent skills two ways, with sharply different scopes.
5	
6	## TL;DR
7	
8	| Scope | Lock file | Where the skill lives | Restored by |
9	|---|---|---|---|
10	| **Global** (every project, every shell) | `~/.agents/.skill-lock.json` (chezmoi-managed) | `~/.agents/skills/<name>/` | `.chezmoiscripts/global/run_onchange_after_40_install_global_skills.sh.tmpl` on every `chezmoi apply` |
11	| **Project** (only inside this repo's working tree, for editing skills) | `./skills-lock.json` (git-tracked) | `./.agents/skills/<name>/` | `.chezmoiscripts/repo/run_onchange_after_45_bootstrap_skills.sh.tmpl` on every `chezmoi apply` (when source dir == repo); manual fallback: `just bootstrap-skills` |
12	
13	The two scopes happen to overlap today (both install
14	`project-knowledge-harness`), but they serve different purposes — see "Why two
15	scopes?" below.
16	
17	## Global scope: must-have skills, on every machine
18	
19	The skills CLI does **not** yet support `npx skills install -g` from a lock
20	file ([upstream issue #283](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills/issues/283),
21	[#549](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills/issues/549)). So we hand-roll
22	restore in two pieces:
23	
24	### `dot_agents/modify_dot_skill-lock.json.tmpl` — the merger
25	
26	A `modify_` script that owns `~/.agents/.skill-lock.json`. Every `chezmoi
27	apply`:
28	
29	1. Reads the live lock file via stdin.
30	2. Merges the **managed-set** declared in `$managed` (top of the script) into
31	   `.skills`, preserving any `installedAt`/`updatedAt`/`skillFolderHash` from
32	   the live entry.
33	3. Preserves any `.skills.<name>` entries **not** in the managed-set (so
34	   ad-hoc `npx skills add … -g` installs survive).
35	4. Preserves `.dismissed` and `.lastSelectedAgents` per-machine state
36	   verbatim.
37	
38	To declare a new must-have global skill, edit the inline `$managed` JSON in
39	that script:
40	
41	```json
42	{
43	  "skills": {
44	    "your-new-skill": {
45	      "source": "owner/repo",
46	      "sourceType": "github",
47	      "sourceUrl": "https://github.com/owner/repo.git",
48	      "skillPath": "skills/your-new-skill/SKILL.md"
49	    }
50	  }
51	}
52	```
53	
54	Then run `chezmoi apply`. The merger writes the new entry into the lock; the
55	restore script (next section) sees the missing on-disk skill and installs it.
56	
57	### `.chezmoiscripts/global/run_onchange_after_40_install_global_skills.sh.tmpl` — the restorer
58	
59	`onchange` hash trigger is the merger script's own SHA256 — so this script
60	re-runs whenever the **managed-set** is edited (not whenever the live lock
61	mutates from random `npx skills update -g` activity).
62	
63	For each entry in `~/.agents/.skill-lock.json`:
64	
65	- If `~/.agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` exists → skip (already installed).
66	- Otherwise → `npx skills add <source> -s <name> -g -y`.
67	
68	This is idempotent: a re-run on a fully-installed machine prints
69	"All globally-managed agent skills present; nothing to install" and exits.
70	
71	### After installing a new skill manually
72	
73	If you `npx skills add foo/bar -g` interactively on a machine and want it to
74	become managed across the fleet:
75	
76	1. `cat ~/.agents/.skill-lock.json` — find the entry the CLI just wrote.
77	2. Copy `source` / `sourceType` / `sourceUrl` / `skillPath` into the
78	   `$managed.skills` block of `dot_agents/modify_dot_skill-lock.json.tmpl`.
79	3. Commit. Other hosts pick it up at next `chezmoi apply`.
80	
81	If you only want it on one machine, do nothing — the merger preserves the
82	live entry on the source machine, and other hosts simply never see it.
83	
84	## Project scope: editing-this-repo convenience
85	
86	`./skills-lock.json` + `./.agents/skills/` exist purely so that **when you're
87	editing the chezmoi repo itself**, agents launched from the repo root can use
88	`project-knowledge-harness` against the repo it documents. They are **not**
89	deployed (chezmoi-ignored: see `.chezmoiignore.tmpl` → `.agents/skills`,
90	`.claude/skills`, `skills-lock.json`) and **not** git-tracked except for
91	`skills-lock.json` (`.gitignore` covers `.agents/`, `.claude/skills/`).
92	
93	Restore is automatic on `chezmoi apply` via
94	`.chezmoiscripts/repo/run_onchange_after_45_bootstrap_skills.sh.tmpl`. The script:
95	
96	1. Checks whether `.chezmoi.sourceDir` contains a `skills-lock.json` (i.e.
97	   this machine's chezmoi source dir IS the repo). If not, exits silently —
98	   project skills only matter when you're editing the repo with an agent.
99	2. Fast-path: if every skill named in the lock already has a
100	   `./.agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`, exits without invoking npx.
101	3. Otherwise runs `npx skills@latest experimental_install` from the source
102	   dir to rebuild `./.agents/skills/...` and `./.claude/skills/...` symlinks.
103	
104	Trigger hash: SHA256 of `skills-lock.json` content, so the script only
105	re-runs when the lock actually changes.
106	
107	Manual fallback (if you want to force a re-bootstrap, or you cloned the repo
108	to a path that isn't your chezmoi source dir):
109	
110	```sh
111	just bootstrap-skills
112	# → npx skills@latest experimental_install
113	```
114	
115	## Why two scopes?
116	
117	| Use case | Where to install |
118	|---|---|
119	| Skill you want available in every project, on every machine | Global (edit `$managed` in the merger script) |
120	| Skill that only makes sense inside this specific repo | Project (`npx skills add ... -y` from repo root, commit `skills-lock.json`) |
121	| Skill you're prototyping locally before deciding | Project, then promote to global once stable |
122	
123	`project-knowledge-harness` is in **both** scopes today because (a) the harness
124	itself targets *any* project so it belongs globally, and (b) we want to use it
125	on the chezmoi repo immediately, which the global install covers but
126	project-scope makes the lock-file dependency explicit for anyone reading
127	`skills-lock.json` here.
128	
129	## How `npx skills` actually wires agents (mechanism reference)
130	
131	Verified by reading [`vercel-labs/skills/src/agents.ts`](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills/blob/main/src/agents.ts)
132	and [`installer.ts`](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills/blob/main/src/installer.ts).
133	Important because the CLI's "I installed your skill for agent X" message does
134	**not** mean agent X actually reads from `~/.agents/skills/` at runtime — that
135	is a per-agent convention, not a guarantee.
136	
137	### Two install strategies
138	
139	| Strategy | What the CLI writes | Agents that use it |
140	|---|---|---|
141	| **Universal** (`skillsDir: '.agents/skills'`) | Nothing in agent-specific dir; agent reads `~/.agents/skills/` (global) or `./.agents/skills/` (project) directly | `cursor`, `opencode`, `codex`, `gemini-cli`, `copilot`, `antigravity`, `warp`, `replit`, `cline`, `kimi-cli`, `firebender`, `deep-agents` |
142	| **Per-agent symlink** | Symlink `~/.<agent>/skills/<name>` → `~/.agents/skills/<name>` (copy on Windows) | `claude-code`, `augment`, `bob`, `cortex`, `crush`, `goose`, `junie`, `kilo`, `kiro`, `kode`, `roo`, `trae`, `windsurf`, etc. |
143	
144	The skip happens at `installer.ts`:
145	
146	```ts
147	if (isGlobal && isUniversalAgent(agentType)) {
148	  return { /* skipped: no symlink, no copy */ };
149	}
150	```
151	
152	So `npx skills add foo -g -a cursor -a opencode` produces **zero** files in
153	`~/.cursor/skills/` or `~/.opencode/skills/`. Whether Cursor and OpenCode
154	actually pick up `~/.agents/skills/foo/SKILL.md` at runtime is up to those
155	agents (Anthropic's Skills spec is Claude Code's; others adopt by convention,
156	not contract).
157	
158	### Lock filename collision (easy to confuse)
159	
160	| Path | Scope | Owner |
161	|---|---|---|
162	| `~/.agents/.skill-lock.json` | Global, **singular** `skill-` | Skills CLI |
163	| `./skills-lock.json` | Project, **plural** `skills-` | Skills CLI |
164	
165	Schema differs (global is v3 with `dismissed`/`lastSelectedAgents`; project is
166	flatter). Don't symlink one to the other.
167	
168	### Restore commands and their quirks
169	
170	| Command | What it does |
171	|---|---|
172	| `npx skills experimental_install` | Restores **project** lock (`./skills-lock.json`) only |
173	| `npx skills experimental_install -g` | `-g` is **silently ignored**, still project-only ([#283](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills/issues/283), [#549](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills/issues/549)) |
174	| `npx skills update -g` | Updates already-installed global skills; does **not** backfill missing entries from the lock |
175	| `npx skills add <source> -s <name> -g -y` | The only working "restore one missing global skill" idiom — what `.chezmoiscripts/global/run_onchange_after_40_install_global_skills.sh.tmpl` loops over |
176	
177	### CLI flag gotchas
178	
179	- **Repo shorthand requires `/skills` suffix when skills live under `skills/`**.
180	  `npx skills add owner/repo` looks at `.agents/skills/` in that repo;
181	  `npx skills add owner/repo/skills` looks at `skills/`. Most third-party skill
182	  repos use the latter layout.
183	- **`-a` does NOT take comma-separated values**. Repeat the flag:
184	  `-a claude-code -a opencode -a cursor`.
185	- **Agent names are normalised** (`claude-code` not `claude`,
186	  `gemini-cli` not `gemini`, `copilot` not `github-copilot`). Run
187	  `npx skills add --list` (or trigger the validation error) to see the
188	  canonical list.
189	
190	### Per-agent env var overrides
191	
192	Agents that respect a custom config dir change where the symlink/skill is
193	read from:
194	
195	| Env var | Default | Effect |
196	|---|---|---|
197	| `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` | `~/.claude` | Skills CLI writes symlinks here instead |
198	| `CODEX_HOME` | `~/.codex` | Codex picks up skills from here (Codex is universal, so the global install relies on `~/.agents/skills/` regardless) |
199	| `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` | `~/.config` | Affects Cursor/OpenCode/Gemini-CLI lookup paths |
200	
201	If you set any of these and re-run `npx skills add -g`, the CLI writes to the
202	new location; chezmoi's lock-file management still uses
203	`~/.agents/.skill-lock.json` (the lock is location-independent).
204	
205	## Anti-patterns
206	
207	- **Don't put skill source files (`.agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`,
208	  templates, etc.) in chezmoi source.** They're owned by the npx skills CLI;
209	  chezmoi managing them creates a constant fight with the CLI's
210	  `skillFolderHash`. Only the **lock file** is chezmoi-managed.
211	- **Don't run `chezmoi re-add ~/.agents/.skill-lock.json`** to capture local
212	  changes. Edit the merger's `$managed` block instead — that's the
213	  source-of-truth list. `re-add` would freeze a snapshot of one machine's
214	  state into the source, defeating the merger's per-machine preservation.
215	- **Don't commit `./.agents/skills/`**. They're skill source clones that the
216	  npx CLI rewrites on every `update`; tracking them creates noisy diffs and
217	  accidental conflicts with upstream skill updates.
218	- **Don't add `-g` to `bootstrap-skills`**. That recipe is project-scope by
219	  design; global is owned by `chezmoi apply`.
220	
221	## References
222	
223	- Live `dot_agents/modify_dot_skill-lock.json.tmpl` — merger source of truth
224	- Live `.chezmoiscripts/global/run_onchange_after_40_install_global_skills.sh.tmpl` — restore loop

我看完了。先給結論再展開細節。

## 目前的實作不是 `npx skills update`，而是「merger + restore」兩步

我們做的事跟 `npx skills update --global -y` **解決的不是同一個問題**。OpenCode 的回答是對的，但它描述的是 `update` 子命令的行為,而我們繞過 `update`/`install` 是因為 issue #283/#549 描述的另一個 gap：**從 lock file 把 *缺失* 的 skill 補回來**(restore from lock)目前 CLI 還做不到。

讓我把兩條路徑釐清,然後再回頭看是否要切換:

### 兩個動作,目前 CLI 對應狀況

| 動作 | CLI 是否原生支援 | 我們怎麼處理 |
|---|---|---|
| **更新已安裝 skill 的內容**(refresh upstream → 重算 hash) | ✅ `npx skills update --global -y` | 沒處理 — 用戶手動跑 / 不跑(install-only invariant) |
| **從 lock file 重建缺失的 skill**(換新機 / 重灌 / 第一次 apply) | ❌ #283/#549 至今未 fix | `dot_agents/modify_dot_skill-lock.json.tmpl` (merger) + `run_onchange_after_40_install_global_skills.sh.tmpl` (逐個 `npx skills add ... -g -y`) |

### 具體如何運作(三個檔案串起來)

**`dot_agents/modify_dot_skill-lock.json.tmpl`** — 純 jq 的 merger,**不呼叫 npx**:

- `modify_` 前綴讓 chezmoi 把 `~/.agents/.skill-lock.json` 現況灌進 stdin,腳本印出新內容到 stdout
- merger 把 inline `$managed` 區塊(目前 `project-knowledge-harness` + `find-skills`)合併進 `.skills`,但**保留** live entry 的 `installedAt`/`updatedAt`/`skillFolderHash`(那些是 CLI 真實安裝狀態的證據)
- **保留** 不在 managed-set 裡的所有條目(本機自己 `npx skills add … -g` 加的不會被洗掉)
- **保留** `.dismissed`/`.lastSelectedAgents`(per-machine state)

**`run_onchange_after_40_install_global_skills.sh.tmpl`** — restore loop:

- Trigger hash 是 merger 腳本自己的 SHA256 → 只有當 `$managed` 改了才重跑(避免 `npx skills update` 改了 hash 就無謂重跑)
- 對 lock 裡每個 entry,檢查 `~/.agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` 是否存在;**缺的才** `npx skills add <source> -s <name> -g -y`
- 全在的話印 "All globally-managed agent skills present" 直接 exit

**Install-only invariant**: 跟整個 repo 一致 — `chezmoi apply` 只**安裝**缺的、不**升級**已有的。實際升級是用戶自己跑 `npx skills update -g`(目前沒有 `just upgrade-skills` recipe,看起來 `scripts/upgrade_tools.sh` 也沒涵蓋)。

### 那要不要改用 `npx skills update --global -y`?

**不要直接替換**,但有兩個 *可能* 的小改進可以考慮:

1. **`update -g` 不回填缺失條目**(docs/tools/agent-skills.md:174 已經記錄: "does **not** backfill missing entries from the lock")。所以即使把 restore 換成 `update -g`,從零開始的新機器/容器照樣不能用 — issue #549 標題就是這個 gap。我們的 `add … -g -y` loop 是目前唯一解。

2. **可以加一個 `just upgrade-skills` recipe** 包成 `npx skills@latest update --global -y`,跟 `upgrade-tools` 系列保持一致(install vs upgrade split)。這個是純 ergonomics,不改現有的 install 流程。要的話我可以開個 `P3 [S]` 進 TODO.md。

3. **驗證一下 issue #549 最新狀態** — 我們的 docs 還停在「未 fix」。如果上游已經 land 了,可以一鍵把 restore 換掉。要我用 WebFetch 看一下 #283/#549 最新留言嗎?

簡短回答你最初的問題:**沒有用 `npx skills update --global -y`**。原因不是疏忽,是 `update` 解決的是「已安裝的 skill 拉新版內容」,我們的腳本解決的是「lock file → 重建缺失 skill」,後者 CLI 還沒做。

## Q1: `update -g` cannot restore missing skills

`runUpdate` → `updateGlobalSkills` (`src/cli.ts:592-710`) iterates lock entries and **never checks disk presence**. The skip condition at `src/cli.ts:619` is `if (!entry.skillFolderHash || !entry.skillPath)` only. For checkable entries it fetches `latestHash` from upstream and reinstalls **only if** `latestHash !== entry.skillFolderHash` (`src/cli.ts:646`). So if `~/.agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` is gone but the lock's stored hash still matches upstream, the entry is **silently skipped** — printed only as "✓ All global skills are up to date" (`src/cli.ts:673`). It is a refresh-in-place, not a restore.

## Q2: Both issues still open; partial workaround landed, full feature unmerged

- **#283** ("`skills install`/`sync` from lock"): **open**, last activity 2026-04-21. The maintainer-suggested workaround is `npx skills experimental_install` — implemented in `src/install.ts` (dispatched at `src/cli.ts:870-874`). But `runInstallFromLock` reads **only** `readLocalLock(cwd)` (`src/install.ts:19`); there is no `-g`/`--global` branch and no path that consults `~/.agents/.skill-lock.json`. So `experimental_install` covers project-level restore, not global.
- **#549** ("`npx skills install` — npm-ci equivalent"): **open**, last activity 2026-04-26.
- **PR #743** "feat: add global restore/relink from .skill-lock.json" — proposes exactly `experimental_install -g`. Status: **open, not merged, mergeable_state=dirty**, last updated 2026-04-10. No other merged PR adds global support.

## Recommendation

**Keep your hand-rolled `npx skills add <source> -s <name> -g -y` loop** in `run_onchange_after_40_install_global_skills.sh.tmpl`. As of main today, neither `update --global -y` (refresh-only) nor `experimental_install` (project-only) restores missing global skills from `~/.agents/.skill-lock.json`. Watch PR #743 — when it merges, the loop collapses to `npx skills experimental_install -g -y`.

It does **not** attempt to install all skills in the lock file, only those whose `skillFolderHash` differs from the server’s `latestHash`.\n\n- Listing actual installed skills is done via the filesystem (e.g. `.agents/skills/<skill-name>` and agent-specific directories in `installer.ts` / `list.ts`), not via the lock file.\n\nSo the lock file is currently acting as a **global registry + update-tracking database**, rather than a declarative “install manifest” like `package.json` or a fully deterministic `package-lock.json`.\n\n### Pain point\n\nBecause the lock file is global and already contains:\n\n- the skill names,\n- the original `sourceUrl` used to install,\n- and the provider/path information,\n\nit *feels* like the perfect place to drive **reproducible installs across machines** or after deletion.\n\nHowever, in practice:\n\n- If I **sync only `~/.agents/.skill-lock.json` via dotfiles** onto a new machine:\n  - For each entry in `lock.skills`:\n   - Uses `entry.sourceUrl` and `name` to **reinstall** that skill via the existing CLI pipeline, e.g.:\n\n     ```bash\n     # Conceptually\n     npx skills <entry.sourceUrl> --skill <name> -g -y\n     ```\n\n3. Optionally supports some modes/flags, for example:\n   - `--missing-only`: only install skills that are not currently present on disk (according to `installer.ts` / `listInstalledSkills`).\n   - `--all`: reinstall *everything* in the lock file regardless of hash (useful for a completely fresh machine).\n   - `--dry-run`: show what would be installed/reinstalled, using lock entries as the source of truth.\n\nThis would provide:\n\n- A **reproducible global skill set across machines** by simply:\n  - syncing `~/.agents/.skill-lock.json` via dotfiles, and\n  - running `npx skills install` on a new machine.\n- A way to **recover from manual deletions** of skill directories without having to remember all original `skills add` commands.\n\nAnd this fits the design because: \n\n- The lock file already holds everything needed to reconstruct the install command:\n  - `sourceUrl` (exact URL originally used),\n  - `source` / `sourceType` / `skillPath` (for future flexibility),\n  - and the skill’s logical name (the key in `lock.skills`).\n- `skills update` already uses this data to drive a reinstall step for updated skills.\n  - `skills install`/`sync` would just generalize this from “only updated skills” to “all skills (or all missing skills) in the lock file”.\n- It keeps the mental model cohesive:\n  - `skills add`: install new skills and write them to the lock file.\n  - `skills check`: read lock file to detect which tracked skills *could* be updated.\n  - `skills update`: read lock file + update only out-of-date skills by reinstalling.\n  - **`skills install` / `skills sync`: read lock file + ensure all tracked skills are *present* on the local machine.**\n\n### Alternatives Considered\n\n_No response_\n\n### Additional Context\n\n### Possible open questions\n\nSome questions I’m not presuming to answer, but worth considering:\n\n- Should `skills install`:\n  -   "body": "### Problem\n\nCurrently, `skills-lock.json` exists to track installed skills and their sources, but there is \nno command to restore skills from it. Running `npx skills update` when no skills are installed \ndoes nothing — it silently exits because the command scans for already-installed skills first \nand then consults the lock file. This makes the lock file useless for reproducible onboarding \nin teams and CI environments.\n\nThe expected workflow for a shared project in a team is:\n1. Developer A installs skills → `skills-lock.json` is generated and committed to the repo\n2. Developer B clones the repo → runs one command to restore all skills\n3. Step 2 is currently impossible without manually scripting `npx skills add <owner/repo>` \n   for every single skill\n\nThis forces teams to either commit the skill files directly (noisy, skills are dependencies \nnot source) or maintain a parallel install script that duplicates what the lock file already \nknows — defeating the purpose of having a lock file at all.\n\n### Proposed Solution\n\nAdd a `npx skills install` command (with `npx skills ci` as a strict alias, mirroring \n`npm install` vs `npm ci`) that:\n\n- Reads `skills-lock.json` from the project root (or `~/.agents/.skill-lock.json` for global)\n- Installs every skill entry in the lock file to its respective agent paths\n- Respects the scope (project vs global) as stored in the lock file\n- Is idempotent — skips skills that are already installed and up-to-date (unless `--force`)\n- Returns a non-zero exit code on failure, making it reliable for CI pipelines\n\nThe lock file already contains all information needed per entry: `sourceUrl`, `skillFolder`, \nand `skillFolderHash`. The install command would simply traverse those entries and invoke \nthe existing install logic.\n\nProposed CLI interface:\n  npx skills install            # install from project-level skills-lock.json\n  npx skills install -g         # install from global ~/.agents/.skill-lock.json\n  npx skills install --force    # reinstall even if already present\n  npx skills ci                 # strict mode: fail if lock file is missing or incomplete\n\n\n### Alternatives Considered\n\n1. Manually scripting `npx skills add` per skill (e.g. in a Makefile or mise task):\n   Works, but requires maintaining a separate script that duplicates what the lock file \n   already tracks. Every time a skill is added or removed, both the lock file and the \n   script need to be updated — a clear violation of the single source of truth principle.\n\n2. Committing skill files directly to the repo:\n   Possible, but skills are generated dependencies — not source code. Committing them adds \n   significant noise to diffs, bloats the repo, and makes updates manual. It's the equivalent \n   of committing `node_modules/`.\n\n3. Issue #134 — `.skills` manifest file:\n   That proposal introduces a new file format for declarative skill installation. This \n   feature request is different and complementary: it proposes using the *existing* \n   `skills-lock.json` structure (no new format needed) to enable restoration, making it \n   immediately useful without any additional configuration.\n\n### Additional Context\n\nThis is the last missing piece for teams treating skills as proper reproducible dependencies:\n\n  # .gitignore\n  .cursor/skills/\n  .claude/skills/\n  .agents/skills/\n  .codex/skills/\n  .agents/skills/\n  # skills-lock.json is committed ✅\n\n  # onboarding / CI — one command:\n  npx skills install\n\nWithout this command, skills-lock.json is only useful for `npx skills update` on machines \nthat already have the skills installed. It provides zero value for fresh clones, new team \nmembers, or clean CI runners.\n\nThis pattern is well-established: npm/yarn/pnpm/bun all use a lock file as the restore mechanism, not just as an update tracker. Skills should be no different.\n\nRelated issues:\n- #134 — `.skills` manifest (different approach, new format)  \n- #337 — project-scoped skills not tracked in lock (a prerequisite for full project-scope support)\n- #371 — `npx skills update` fails silently (same root: update assumes skills exist)",

_**Agent - sidechain (claude-opus-4-7 2026-04-27 09:40:28Z)**_

## Q1: `update -g` cannot restore missing skills

`runUpdate` → `updateGlobalSkills` (`src/cli.ts:592-710`) iterates lock entries and **never checks disk presence**. The skip condition at `src/cli.ts:619` is `if (!entry.skillFolderHash || !entry.skillPath)` only. For checkable entries it fetches `latestHash` from upstream and reinstalls **only if** `latestHash !== entry.skillFolderHash` (`src/cli.ts:646`). So if `~/.agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` is gone but the lock's stored hash still matches upstream, the entry is **silently skipped** — printed only as "✓ All global skills are up to date" (`src/cli.ts:673`). It is a refresh-in-place, not a restore.

## Q2: Both issues still open; partial workaround landed, full feature unmerged

- **#283** ("`skills install`/`sync` from lock"): **open**, last activity 2026-04-21. The maintainer-suggested workaround is `npx skills experimental_install` — implemented in `src/install.ts` (dispatched at `src/cli.ts:870-874`). But `runInstallFromLock` reads **only** `readLocalLock(cwd)` (`src/install.ts:19`); there is no `-g`/`--global` branch and no path that consults `~/.agents/.skill-lock.json`. So `experimental_install` covers project-level restore, not global.
- **#549** ("`npx skills install` — npm-ci equivalent"): **open**, last activity 2026-04-26.
- **PR #743** "feat: add global restore/relink from .skill-lock.json" — proposes exactly `experimental_install -g`. Status: **open, not merged, mergeable_state=dirty**, last updated 2026-04-10. No other merged PR adds global support.

## Recommendation

**Keep your hand-rolled `npx skills add <source> -s <name> -g -y` loop** in `run_onchange_after_40_install_global_skills.sh.tmpl`. As of main today, neither `update --global -y` (refresh-only) nor `experimental_install` (project-only) restores missing global skills from `~/.agents/.skill-lock.json`. Watch PR #743 — when it merges, the loop collapses to `npx skills experimental_install -g -y`.

驗證完了,直接回答你的三個問題:

### Q1: `update -g` 對「lock 有但磁碟沒裝」的 skill 行為

**Ignore 並 silently skip**。`src/cli.ts:619` 的 skip 條件只看 lock entry 自己的 metadata(`!entry.skillFolderHash || !entry.skillPath`),**完全不檢查 `~/.agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` 是否存在於磁碟上**。

走完 update flow 之後,如果 lock 的 hash 跟 upstream 還對得上,它印一句 "✓ All global skills are up to date" 就走了 — 你的硬碟其實是空的,但 CLI 不會發現也不會補。

→ 它是 **refresh-in-place**,不是 restore。我們 docs 裡寫的「does **not** backfill missing entries from the lock」是對的。

357	# Run `chezmoi update --init` (or apply / diff) across many remote hosts in

360	# sources: plain / interactive prompt / Bitwarden CLI / none.
361	# Per-host log: logs/fleet-apply/<UTC-timestamp>/<host>.log
362	# Exit code = number of failed hosts.

372

374	# Use this in vibe loops to see exactly what your latest commit will do

377	    ./scripts/fleet_apply.py --dry-run --hosts {{HOST}} --serial {{ARGS}}

379	# Apply ONLY a single chezmoi target on each host (skips ansible / Brewfile).
380	# PATH is the chezmoi target path, e.g. `.config/zsh/aliases.zsh` or
381	# `.zshrc`. Fast feedback for editing one dotfile across the fleet without
382	# waiting for full Linuxbrew/ansible cycles. Pass extra `--hosts HOST` to
383	# scope. Internally sets CHEZMOI_FLEET_APPLY_PATH so the wrapper runs
384	# `chezmoi apply <relpath>` instead of `chezmoi update --init`.
385	fleet-apply-file PATH *ARGS:

388	# Apply a feature BRANCH instead of pulling main. Each remote does
389	# `git fetch origin BRANCH && git checkout -B BRANCH origin/BRANCH &&
390	# git merge --ff-only origin/BRANCH` before chezmoi apply. Fails loud
391	# on divergence — use `just fleet-apply-branch-force` to nuke local
392	# state with `git reset --hard`. Local hosts skip this entirely (source
393	# is your editor's working tree).
394	fleet-apply-branch BRANCH *ARGS:
395	    ./scripts/fleet_apply.py --branch {{BRANCH}} {{ARGS}}
396	
397	# Like fleet-apply-branch but uses `git reset --hard origin/BRANCH` on
398	# remotes, destroying any local divergence. Use after force-pushing a
399	# rebased topic branch so every host follows.
400	fleet-apply-branch-force BRANCH *ARGS:
401	    ./scripts/fleet_apply.py --branch {{BRANCH}} --force-checkout {{ARGS}}
402

406

408	fleet-apply-kill *ARGS:

410	
411	# Probe each host for running chezmoi/ansible (use after killing local SSH)
412	fleet-apply-status *ARGS:
413	    ./scripts/fleet_apply.py --status {{ARGS}}
414	
415	# Like fleet-apply-status but re-poll every Ns until everyone is idle
416	# (Ctrl+C to stop). Default interval 10s; override with --watch=N in ARGS.
417	fleet-apply-watch *ARGS:
